title: GraphQL Mutations
description: Learn how to modify data with GraphQL mutations

questions.explanation: A GraphQL mutation is a request to modify data on the server, such as creating, updating, or deleting records.
questions.hint: It's the opposite of a query

questions.text: How do mutations differ from queries?
questions.explanation: Mutations are for modifying data, queries are for reading. Mutations can have side effects, queries should be side-effect-free.
A mutation can return any type defined in the schema, including the modified object, success status, or list of results.

questions.text: What is a mutation input type?
questions.explanation: An input type is a special type used to group input parameters for mutations, like CreateUserInput with name and email fields.
acceptable_answers: a type for grouping input parameters

questions.explanation: Mutations should be sequential because they have side effects and order matters - one mutation might depend on another.
